bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary announces setting up of women-only university
bihar_raw_news.content: ANI Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary announces plans for a 'Mahila Vishwavidyalaya', with women as faculty, students and non-teaching staff. Patna: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Thursday said the state will have a ' Mahila Vishwavidyalaya ', a university in which the faculty, students as well as non-teaching staff will all be women. He made the announcement at a function in the state capital where a sum of Rs 600 crore was disbursed among beneficiaries, through DBT, under the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana which was rolled out last year. "I extend my greetings to all sisters of Bihar on the eve of Raksha Bandhan. We believe that the state can prosper only if our women do well... A Mahila Vishwavidyalaya will be set up in the state. The university will be run by women, from top to bottom. The vice chancellor, professors, other staffers and students shall all be women," the chief minister said. Also read: Bihar CM Samrat Chaudhary agrees to single-phase teachers' recruitment exam amid protests The function was also marked by the signing of an MoU between the state's Department for Excise and Prohibition and the Prajapita Brahma Kumari Ishwariya Vishwavidyalaya for spreading public awareness over the ills of consumption of intoxicants. Live Events Additionally, loans were also distributed among 10,000 beneficiaries from the JEEViKA Fund . Stressing that the government was committed to making women self-reliant and economically empowered, Choudhary said a target has been set to identify 10 lakh JEEViKA Didis and install solar panels at their homes by March 31 next year. JEEViKA Didis will also be associated with the deaddiction campaign to keep people away from intoxicants through street plays and other means, he added. The chief minister extended his best wishes to 7,376 women selected through the nurse recruitment examination conducted by the Bihar Public Service Commission, an official statement read. Choudhary highlighted that under the Chief Minister Balika PhD Fellowship , around 1,000 female students will receive financial assistance of Rs 10,000 per month for four years to pursue higher education and research - a decision that was announced by him on Wednesday. He lamented that there were only 600 women among 4,600 individuals pursuing PhD studies in Bihar. Add as a Reliable and Trusted News Source Add Now! bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Student Protests: Why Government Jobs Matter - Frontline
bihar_raw_news.content: DIGITAL EXCLUSIVE Bihar’s job aspirants run out of patience As BPSC protests turn violent in Patna, economists and opposition leaders point to two decades of stalled recruitment behind the anger. Published : Aug 27, 2026 19:58 IST - 7 MINS READ Anand Mishra Anand Mishra currently serves as Political Editor, Frontline. AI Summary COMMents SHARE Copy link Email Facebook Twitter Telegram LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit READ LATER SEE ALL Remove Students in Patna on August 25, during a march from Gandhi Maidan to Raj Bhavan demanding the cancellation of the 70th BPSC examination. | Photo Credit: Rahul Sharma/ANI On August 25, when student protests in Patna turned violent—from dancing, bathing, and shampooing in front of water cannons to breaking barricades and pelting stones—the episode set off a political storm. But the causes run deeper. This is not the first student protest Bihar has seen in recent years. Its significance lies in timing: it follows the CJP -led protest against NEET-UG paper leaks at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi in June-July, and the protest over irregularities in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission examination in Ranchi in July-August. In Bihar, the protesters are aspirants of the Bihar Public Service Commission, who allege that the exam was compromised by a paper leak and are demanding it be cancelled. The protests began when prelims exams were conducted and continue to date even after the completion of exams in June. The other protesters, who demanded that the proposed two-phased format of the Teacher Recruitment Examination-4 should be changed to a single phase, also joined. They are alleging irregularties in all recruitment exams. In all three protests, the underlying fear is the loss of job opportunities. In the two protests in the undivided Bihar region— Jharkhand was part of Bihar until 2000—the fear is more specific: losing a government job, of which there are already too few. With private-sector jobs scarce and few avenues to build entrepreneurial skills in the two Hindi-belt States, a government job remains the dream. Santosh Mehrotra, a former professor of economics at the Centre for Labour, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and co-author of the recent book India Out of Work: Rethinking India’s Growth Story , says protests over paper leaks and government appointments are nothing new. “Since the BJP came to power in India, if there have been 152 such paper leaks, should protests be surprising? The Bihar government of [then] Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, in power for 20 years, mostly with BJP support, did not make many appointments of teachers or health staff for two decades. Vacancies run into lakhs. Recent teacher appointments are, for the second time in three years, causing aspirants to return to the streets—over the recruitment exam’s design and over whether only Bihari domiciles should be considered,” he told Frontline . bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar first state to have 50 lakh 'lakhpati didis', says CM Samrat - ANI News
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar first state to have 50 lakh 'lakhpati didis', says CM Samrat ANI | Updated: Aug 27, 2026 17:50 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna ( Bihar ) [India], August 27 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Thursday said that the state has become the first in the country to achieve the milestone of 50 lakh women becoming 'Lakhpati Didis' through various livelihood initiatives. Addressing the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rozgar Yojana programme in Patna, Choudhary said that financial assistance was provided to 1.81 crore women under the scheme, and many beneficiaries used the funds to start or expand income-generating activities. "The funds were distributed to 1.81 crore sisters. Our data shows that approximately 37 per cent, around 25 to 27 lakh sisters, used the money for activities like animal husbandry," the Bihar Chief Minister said. He added that around 18 per cent of women beneficiaries entered the agriculture sector, while several others started manufacturing activities and worked towards developing markets for their products. Highlighting the impact of livelihood programmes, Choudhary said that three lakh 'Jeevika Didis' are earning an annual income of more than Rs 2 lakh. "Over 10 lakh sisters are integrating three different types of livelihood activities. Another 25 lakh sisters are engaged in two varieties of livelihood activities, ranging from goat rearing to operating pushcarts or other small-scale ventures, while approximately 12 lakh sisters are currently engaged in a single type of employment," he said. The Chief Minister said that the government will now shift its focus towards creating a dedicated system to identify and track women who have achieved the 'Lakhpati Didi' status. "While we will continue to support families, we must create a system that specifically tracks and distinguishes these 'Lakhpati Didis' to understand exactly how many of our sisters have achieved this status," Choudhary said. The 'Lakhpati Didi' initiative aims to promote financial independence among women by encouraging self-employment and sustainable livelihood opportunities through self-help groups and other support mechanisms. The Bihar Chief Minister said that the achievement reflects the success of women-centric development programmes in the state and emphasised the need to further strengthen livelihood opportunities for women across Bihar . Earlier, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Thursday said that educated and self-reliant women are the foundation of a developed and prosperous Bihar , emphasising the need to provide girls with quality education, skills and better opportunities. The Chief Minister laid the foundation stone for the construction of a G+6 science block and auditorium at Magadh Mahila College in Patna. He also interacted with students and discussed their academic needs, aspirations and suggestions. Addressing the gathering, CM Choudhary said, "The progress of women is the progress of Bihar . Providing quality education, modern facilities and opportunities to daughters and sisters is essential for building a developed Bihar ." (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.content: How Bihar’s Pink Bus service is helping women travel more easily Impact assessment survey reveals that 56% of women said they now feel more confident travelling on their own, most using it for education and work. Join Our WhatsApp Channel Surabhi Updated Aug 27, 2026 4:02 PM IST Women who shifted to the Pink Bus from autos and e-rickshaws report a 28 to 35% cut in daily travel costs While several states have rolled out schemes to enable easier public transport for women, a new study on Bihar’s dedicated bus service for women reveals that it has made travel for women safer, more accessible and cheaper. The Pink Bus initiative was announced in the Bihar State Budget 2025-26 with two core aims – improving safe and accessible mobility for women and providing pathways to include women in the transport supply side. While it is not a free service with fares ranging from ₹6 to ₹25, depending on the distance, the study found that in just two months of its launch, the ridership reached 33,000. It also hires women conductors, providing an additional source of employment. bihar_raw_news.content: Updated 27 August 2026 at 10:13 IST Nepal’s deadly flash floods trigger alerts across UP and Bihar as 20 NDRF teams are deployed amid fears of rising Gandak waters. Asian News International India News 4 min read Follow : UP-Bihar Border Villages on Alert Following Nepal Floods; Waterlogged Roads Disrupt Connectivity | Image: X Kushinagar: Following the flood tragedy in Nepal, an atmosphere of fear prevailed in the Uttar Pradesh-Bihar border in Kushinagar district. However, as floodwaters did not enter overnight, villagers breathed a sigh of relief in the morning. However, due to heavy rainwater accumulation along the routes connecting Shivpur, Basantpur, and Marchahwa villages in Kushinagar district and Bihar, small streams and drains overflowed, spilling water across the roads. Villagers were seen wading through the waterlogged roads, holding their footwear in their hands. Furthermore, due to the high water levels, the movement of small vehicles was completely halted, forcing villagers to rely on tractor-trolleys for commuting. Local administrations in nearby areas have issued warnings via loudspeakers asking residents to move their belongings and livestock to higher ground amid reports of water release from Nepal. Advertisement Detailing the situation on the ground, Guddu Sahani, a resident of Basantpur, said that while floodwaters have not entered homes yet, the low causeway has created severe travel hurdles. "We received information that the water has been released from Nepal. So far, I haven't heard anything directly from the administration about what they are saying. Moreover, no official has visited our village yet... As for any danger... floodwaters haven't arrived yet up to this point. The water that has accumulated here was because the causeway and road were constructed a bit too low. If the water level rises just a little more, boats will start operating. Then we will have to pay Rs 20, Rs 30, Rs 40, or Rs 50 per trip just to commute back and forth," Sahani said. Durgawati Devi, another resident from Basantpur, pointed out the practical difficulties faced by villagers following the administration's alert. Advertisement "Some were saying that we should flee to higher ground along with our cattle and livestock. But if our house is in this waterlogged area, where else will we stay? We have to stay here in the water. We are still here. The administration made announcements yesterday. We heard it over the loudspeakers. We live in Basantpur. They didn't come to Kushinagar side, but they were announcing in Sohagibarwa, so we heard it from there. Right now, the water level is stable; the fresh floodwater hasn't reached this side yet," she said. Shobhawati, a resident of Marchahwa, stated that villagers remained awake throughout the night keeping watch over water levels. "The water level remains the same as earlier; it is stagnant. bihar_raw_news.content: Home / India News / From Rasuwa to Bihar: How Nepal's flash floods can travel into India From Rasuwa to Bihar: How Nepal's flash floods can travel into India A flash flood in Nepal's Rasuwa district has raised flood concerns in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. Here's how the Trishuli-Narayani-Gandak river system connects Nepal to India An aerial view of flood affected Bhotekoshi river at Benighat area, in Dhading district, Nepal. (Photo: PTI) Rimjhim Singh New Delhi 10 min read Last Updated : Aug 27 2026 | 2:24 PM IST Listen to This Article A deadly flash flood in Nepal’s Rasuwa district on Wednesday has raised concerns in parts of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh , with authorities monitoring potential rises in downstream water levels. The disaster has killed 165 people, while many others, including more than 300 Indian tourists, remain missing. The affected area is around 160 kilometres from the Indian border, but its effects can extend into India because of the region’s interconnected river systems. Several major Himalayan rivers originate in or pass through Nepal before entering India and flowing across the Gangetic plains. A sudden increase in water levels upstream can therefore affect areas downstream, even after the flood wave crosses an international border. On Wednesday, the Centre said it recorded a sudden rise in the Trishuli river at Furke Khola in Nepal following a suspected flash flood or glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) near the Nepal-China border. The Central Water Commission (CWC) said the resulting water surge could move downstream through the Gandak river in India. This prompted Bihar and Uttar Pradesh to take precautionary measures. However, a flood in one part of Nepal does not pose the same risk to every part of northern India. The impact depends on the river basin involved. In the current case, the important river link is from the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers to the Narayani and then the Gandak in India. What happened in Nepal? According to the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), a flash flood hit Rasuwa district on the morning of August 26. A large surge of water, sediment and boulders moved through the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river systems. bihar_raw_news.content: SIGN IN Edition IN IN US Download App Follow Us On: News India Bihar on high alert as Nepal floods swell river Gandak, all 36 barrage gates opened Bihar on high alert as Nepal floods swell river Gandak, all 36 barrage gates opened Floodwaters from Nepal entered the Gandak river system, prompting Bihar to open all 36 barrage gates. The move has triggered round-the-clock monitoring and emergency preparations across vulnerable districts. Advertisement An aerial view of swollen Bhotekoshi river in Nepal's Dhading district. (Photo: PTI) India Today News Desk Patna , UPDATED: Aug 27, 2026 07:30 IST Bihar was put on high alert on Wednesday after floodwaters from Nepal entered river Gandak and reached the Gandak Barrage, prompting authorities to open all 36 gates to manage the surge, officials said. Around 1.50 lakh cusecs of water had been released from the barrage by 11 pm, the highest discharge recorded there during the day. Officials said the flow was now expected to start receding. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story The alert in Bihar came after a massive flash flood originating in Tibet swept through central Nepal, killing over 150 people and leaving more than 750 missing, including 133 Indian nationals. Several towns and villages were hit, key bridges were washed away and about a dozen hydropower projects were crippled. The Gandak Barrage is located at Valmikinagar in West Champaran, Bihar's northernmost district bordering Nepal. Nepal Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told Parliament that an earthquake struck the Tibet region at 8:37 am (local time) and flash floods were reported three minutes later, suggesting the tremors may have caused a glacial outburst that triggered the floods. As soon as the news broke, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary held a meeting with Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit and other senior officials to review the situation. Officials were directed to remain on high alert, take necessary measures and keep continuous watch on developments. Amrit also held a meeting with district magistrates and senior police officials of the bordering districts, and district authorities were told to complete all rescue and relief preparations and closely monitor the situation. Water Resources Department secretary Chandrashekhar Singh said, "The situation is expected to remain normal. Nevertheless, all teams are on alert at the barrage, along the embankments and in the control room." The highest discharge recorded this year was 2.24 lakh cusecs on July 14, 2026, while 5.625 lakh cusecs was recorded on September 28, 2024. In a post on X, Choudhary said the loss of lives in Nepal was deeply saddening. "My deepest condolences to the families of those who have passed away in this disaster. I pray to God that all Indian citizens stranded in Nepal remain safe and secure," he said. bihar_raw_news.title: From Bihar's makhana to Rajasthan's jamun and Maharashtra's tofu, PMFME Bazaar ... - DD India
bihar_raw_news.content: Top Stories of the Day Share DD India August 27, 2026 1:40 PM IST Rajasthan | Maharashtra | Bihar | Makhana | PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises | Micro Food Processing Bazaar | jamun | tofu | PMFME Bazaar | grassroots food entrepreneurs From Bihar’s makhana to Rajasthan’s jamun and Maharashtra’s tofu, PMFME Bazaar showcases India’s grassroots food entrepreneurs Author: DD India From makhana-based cookies in Bihar and preservative-free jamun products made with the help of tribal women in Rajasthan to tofu innovations in Maharashtra and millet processing in Odisha, the PMFME (Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises) Bazaar in the national capital showcased how small food enterprises are turning local ingredients, traditional knowledge and grassroots entrepreneurship into businesses with wider markets. Organised by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries at the India Habitat Centre on August 24 and 25, the PMFME Bazaar brought together exhibitors from 25 States and Union Territories. The two-day event provided micro food processing enterprises, self-help groups (SHGs), farmer producer organisations (FPOs), cooperatives and entrepreneurs a platform to showcase their products, interact with buyers and explore new markets. The stalls featured a wide variety of products, ranging from millets, spices and pickles to snacks, beverages and other value-added foods, reflecting India’s diverse culinary traditions. More than a marketplace, the Bazaar highlighted the ways in which local ingredients and traditional practices can be developed into modern products and brands capable of reaching consumers beyond their regions. Launched on June 29, 2020, the PMFME Scheme provides financial, technical and business support to micro food processing enterprises, helping entrepreneurs establish new units or strengthen existing businesses. The stories of entrepreneurs showcased at the Bazaar offered a glimpse into the impact of such support on businesses operating at very different scales and in different parts of the country. Bihar’s makhana gets a modern identity For Faraz and his team at SHHE Foods Private Limited, the Bazaar was an opportunity to showcase a journey that began in Bihar with a simple idea – giving the state’s much-loved makhana a modern identity. SHHE Foods started its operations in 2021, experimenting with value-added makhana products. Among its innovations were makhana-infused cookies and smaller, convenient packs designed for easy consumption. The enterprise associated with the PMFME Scheme in the same year. According to the account shared at the Bazaar, the association helped strengthen the company’s visibility and brand-building efforts while opening up new business opportunities. The Bazaar itself has emerged as an important platform for the enterprise to establish customer and business connections. PMFME support also helped the company upgrade its processing unit. Under the scheme’s credit-linked capital subsidy, which provides 35 per cent of the total project cost up to Rs 10 lakh per unit, SHHE Foods received more than Rs 3 lakh in subsidy against a Rs 10 lakh loan. bihar_raw_news.title: Nepal flash flood raises concern in Bihar as Gandak level comes under watch
bihar_raw_news.content: PATNA — A devastating flash flood in Nepal’s Rasuwa district has raised concerns in Bihar because of the interconnected river system linking the two regions. The floodwaters entered the Bhote Koshi River from the Tibet region before flowing into the Trishuli River and eventually the Narayani, which is known as the Gandak after entering India. The Nepal flood occurred around 9 a.m. on Wednesday, causing extensive damage in areas including Timure, Syaphrubesi and Rasuwagadhi. Roads, bridges and other infrastructure were washed away, while a large number of people were reported missing. Nepali authorities said the sudden surge originated in Tibet, with preliminary assessments suggesting that an obstruction caused by glacial debris may have given way suddenly. According to an official, the river route can be broadly traced as the Tibet, Bhote Koshi, Trishuli, Narayani, Gandak, and Ganga Rivers. "The development has prompted increased monitoring of the Gandak River in Bihar. However, the occurrence of flooding in Nepal does not automatically mean that Bihar will face immediate flooding. The impact will depend on the volume of water moving downstream, rainfall, contributions from other rivers and the manner in which barrages regulate the flow," an official said. The Gandak enters Bihar through Valmikinagar in West Champaran, making the Valmikinagar Barrage particularly important in regulating the river's flow. The official further said that the districts requiring close monitoring include West Champaran, as the areas around Valmikinagar and the Gandak basin could face increased pressure if water levels rise. In East Champaran, low-lying and riverside areas may face greater risks of flooding and erosion. The Gopalganj district, which is adjoining the West and East Champaran, could face a flood threat due to a sudden increase in Gandak water discharge. The low-lying areas connected to the Gandak system require monitoring in the Siwan district, as it is adjoining the Gopalganj district.

bihar_raw_news.content: Leaders across party lines express concern, grief over devastating Nepal flash floods IANS August 27, 2026 11:50 AM Share on | New Delhi, Aug 27 (IANS) Leaders across party lines on Thursday expressed grief and concern over the devastating flash floods in Nepal, describing the tragedy as deeply saddening and painful while stressing the need for relief, rescue efforts and continued vigilance in neighbouring Indian states. The reactions came as the bodies of 162 people swept away by a massive flash flood in Nepal's Bhote Koshi River had been recovered as of Thursday morning. The disaster has caused widespread devastation, with several people still reported missing and extensive damage inflicted on property and infrastructure. Speaking to IANS, Bihar Minister Ram Kripal Yadav said the tragedy in Nepal was extremely distressing and had resulted in significant loss of lives and property. "The tragedy in Nepal is very saddening. There was a sudden flood and Nepal has been devastated. Indians are also missing. Both lives and property have been lost. It is deeply saddening and a matter of great concern. Our respected Prime Minister Narendra Modi has spoken to the Prime Minister of Nepal and assured him of all possible support," he said. BJP Bihar President Sanjay Saraogi termed the situation a terrible disaster, saying heavy rains and flooding had caused severe destruction. "There has been a terrible disaster in Nepal. Dams have been destroyed and heavy rains have caused severe damage. More than 1,000 people are still missing in Nepal. Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke to the Prime Minister of Nepal and assured the people of Nepal that India would provide all possible assistance," he said. Bihar Assembly Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav described the incident as extremely painful and called for greater vigilance in Bihar in view of possible repercussions on river systems. "We saw the videos yesterday showing the way the floodwaters rose and people were running for safety. We feel the Bihar government needs to keep a closer watch on the situation. Everyone needs to remain alert. There is also concern that the Gandak River could be affected in Bihar," he said. Shiv Sena spokesperson Shaina NC offered condolences to the families of those who lost their lives and raised concerns about tourists from Maharashtra stranded in Nepal. bihar_raw_news.title: If there is a flood in Tibet, why should Bihar worry? - India Today
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Information If there is a flood in Tibet, why should Bihar worry? If there is a flood in Tibet, why should Bihar worry? A flood in Tibet may seem far removed from Bihar, but the two are connected by the Himalayan river system. The Bhotekoshi flows into the Sun Kosi, which becomes part of the Kosi system before entering Bihar. advertisement A flood in Tibet can have consequences far downstream. Here is how the Bhotekoshi connects Tibet to the Kosi river system and why Bihar keeps a close watch on Himalayan floods. (Photo - X/@@XueJia24682) India Today Information Desk New Delhi, UPDATED: Aug 27, 2026 13:31 IST A flood in Tibet may sound like a distant event for people in Bihar. But when it involves rivers flowing through the Himalayas, the two regions are far more connected than they appear. The Bhotekoshi river, which originates in the Tibetan region and flows through Nepal, is part of the larger river system that eventually feeds the Kosi. The Kosi then enters Bihar, where it has a long history of causing destructive floods. So, why should Bihar worry when heavy rain or flooding occurs upstream? The answer lies in how Himalayan rivers carry water downstream across borders, and how quickly conditions in the upper catchment can affect areas much farther away. advertisement Read More Nepal Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said 175 people have died in the devastating flash floods that swept through Nepal and neighbouring Tibet, while nearly 300 Indians are among those reported missing. Most of the missing Indians are believed to be tourists and pilgrims travelling towards the Kailash Mansarovar region. (Photo: PTI) THE FIRST LINK BHOTEKOSHI, AND HOW DOES TIBET CONNECT TO BIHAR? The Bhotekoshi river, which originates in the Tibetan Himalayan region, flows into Nepal and joins the Sun Kosi. The Sun Kosi is one of the major rivers that, along with the Arun and Tamur, forms the Saptakoshi river system. The Saptakoshi then flows southwards into India, where it becomes the Kosi and passes through northern Bihar before meeting the Ganga near Kursela in Katihar district. advertisement This interconnected river system means heavy rain or flooding in the upper Himalayan catchment can have consequences much farther downstream, including in Bihar. (Photo: PTI) WHY DOES BIHAR FEAR THE KOSI? The Kosi is famously known as the “Sorrow of Bihar” because of its history of destructive floods. The river carries a huge amount of water and sediment from the Himalayas. Its course has also shifted repeatedly over the centuries, creating a difficult flood-management challenge for the plains of north Bihar. Districts including Supaul, Saharsa, Madhepura, Araria and Purnea are among those that have faced serious Kosi flooding. (Photo: PTI) THE 2008 FLOOD SHOWED WHAT CAN HAPPEN The 2008 Kosi flood remains one of the clearest reminders of the river's destructive potential. A breach near Kusaha in Nepal caused the Kosi to change its course, inundating large areas of north Bihar. Millions of people were affected by the disaster. advertisement

bihar_raw_news.content: NDRF on high alert as Nepal flash flood threatens Gandak; Bihar, UP deploy rescue teams in vulnerable areas ANI | Updated: Aug 27, 2026 03:37 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], August 27 (ANI): A sudden flash flood in Nepal and a glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) near the Nepal -China border have triggered heightened flood preparedness across Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, with the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) deploying 20 teams in the two states and authorities closely monitoring the likely downstream movement of floodwaters through the Gandak river . The NDRF has placed its teams on high alert amid the possibility that the flood wave generated in Nepal could travel downstream through the Gandak river and affect vulnerable districts in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. NDRF Commandant Gyaneshwar Singh said a GLOF had affected the Tibet- Nepal border and the floodwater was subsequently moving further downstream in Nepal . "A GLOF (glacial lake outburst flood) hit the Tibet- Nepal border and then further down in Nepal . It is likely to hit Gandak. Since our responsibility is up to the India- Nepal border, MHA is monitoring it. The state government is also assessing the situation," Singh told ANI. According to the NDRF, a sudden rise in the water level of the Trishuli river at Furke Khola in Nepal , around 160 kilometres from the Indian border, has been reported amid suspected GLOF activity near the Nepal -China border. The Central Water Commission has advised authorities in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh near the India- Nepal border to remain alert and maintain close monitoring of the Gandak river . The NDRF said that, keeping in view the anticipated flood situation in the Gandak river , it was on high alert. Two NDRF teams have been dispatched to Bihar 's West Champaran and Muzaffarpur districts, both located in the Gandak river basin. The deployment followed an assessment of the developing situation by the Bihar government. "Two of our teams have been deployed in the Gandak river basin - West Champaran and Muzaffarpur. The area likely to be hit in UP, Kushinagar lies beside Gandak. So, we have deployed our teams," Singh said. He said nine NDRF teams were now deployed in Bihar and another 11 in Uttar Pradesh for flood warning and response operations. "Already, 9 of our teams are deployed in Bihar and 11 in UP for floodwater rescue. MHA is monitoring the overall situation. State Governments and Central Water Commission are also monitoring it. An advisory was issued in the morning to the state Governments," Singh said. He added that additional NDRF teams were ready and could be deployed based on the requirements assessed by the respective state governments. "Our additional teams are also prepared. As and when State Governments feel that we are required, NDRF will deploy the team," he said. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that the government is fully committed to creating a modern sports ecosystem for India in the 21st century. He said that, from sports universities to modern training centres, an ecosystem is being developed across the country where talent receives support at every stage. Addressing the Khelo India Dialogue through video conferencing today, Mr Modi said that sports is not limited merely to winning medals, rather, it is a mission to unite India’s sporting prowess and youth power in the building of a developed India. He said every district has the potential to shine on the global sports map. The Prime Minister said he had announced from the ramparts of the Red Fort that a big talent hunt to identify kids from 5 to 15 years of age in sports. He emphasised the need to focus not only on the sport a child is interested in but also on identifying the sport they are best suited for. The Prime Minister assured to provide all possible support from the government for this. The Prime Minister expressed happiness that today sports has emerged as an excellent career and profession in India. Mr Modi said sports does not just teach to become champions but also to become better competitors. He said, ‘The Khelo India Samvad is not merely a program for discussing sports, but it is a platform for dialogue where every single idea can give a new direction to the nation’s sports vision. ‘Prime Minister said that these new ideas from the power of the country’s youth will become the strength that helps realise the vision of Viksit Bharat. Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Mansukh Mandaviya said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi, sports has emerged as a national priority and an important instrument of youth empowerment. He said India’s sports ecosystem is now moving beyond infrastructure and medals as initiatives such as the Fit India Movement and Sunday on Cycle encourage citizens to make fitness a part of everyday life. The Minister said that the National Sports Governance Act is promoting transparency and accountability and strengthening fair opportunities in sports so that talented sportspersons receive an equal platform to demonstrate their abilities. Dr Mandaviya said the government’s approach is aimed at making India’s youth active partners in the journey towards a Viksit Bharat. The Programme was organised as part of the National Sports Day 2026 celebrations by Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat). It was conducted across the country with participation of youth at two colleges in every district across States and Union Territories. The event brought together sports, youth leadership, civic responsibility, volunteering, fitness and nation-building on a common platform. The Khelo India Dialogue provided a direct channel for young people to engage with the country’s sporting ambitions while ensuring that their ideas and perspectives become part of the continuing conversation on India’s youth and sports ecosystem. The Khelo India Dialogue is being held in line with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of building a fit, disciplined and sporting nation and placing the aspirations of youth at the centre of the national development agenda.

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | International 679 Nepal flash flood claims nearly 160 lives; over 750 Missing, including 133 Indians
national_raw_news.content: In Nepal, nearly 160 people have been killed and over 750, including 133 Indian nationals, remain missing after a massive flash flood swept through central Nepal yesterday. Originating in Tibet, the flood devastated several towns and villages, washing away critical bridges and crippling a dozen hydropower projects. Nepal Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told the parliament that an earthquake hit the Tibet region at 8:37 am (local time) and the flash floods were reported three minutes later, suggesting a glacial outburst due to tremors, which triggered the floods. Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said the massive flood entered the Trishuli River through the Bhote Koshi in Timure, a border town in Rasuwa district, due to the rockslide and swelling of the Lhende River situated along the Nepal-Tibet border. It then spread along the river course to other districts like Nuwakot, Chitwan, Gorkha, Tanahu and Nawalparasi East, covering areas ranging to nearly 2 hundred kilometres from the capital Kathmandu. The Nepal Police in a social media post said 157 people died in the flash flood. The Nepal government said around 500 people were missing. According to China’s state-run news channel, 3 people were dead and 265 were missing on the Chinese side of the border. Videos from the affected areas showed a powerful surge of muddy water, rocks and debris sweeping through the border region. Officials said that around 100 people have been rescued from different parts of the affected areas. Of them, 30 are undergoing treatment at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital in Kathmandu. Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke to his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah and assured him of all possible humanitarian assistance. Mr Shah thanked Prime Minister Modi for his warm words of solidarity and for offering humanitarian assistance. New Delhi has already sent the first tranche of relief supplies to the neighbouring nation. The Indian Embassy in Kathmandu issued emergency numbers for assistance and information related to Indian nationals. The numbers are: +977 985 131 6807 and +977 970 910 7500. The Nepal Tourism Board also issued similar numbers, including the toll-free emergency number 1234, hotline 1144 and Tourist Police number 9851289445 for help. The Embassy of India in Beijing also issued a helpline number – 0086 185 1428 4905, which can also be contacted through WhatsApp. At least 50 of the Indians missing were pilgrims for the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra. Several Indian states – including Uttar Pradesh and Keralam have also issued helpline numbers. Other than the Indians and NRIs, the remaining missing tourists were from more than two dozen countries, including the US, Malaysia, the UK, South Africa, Australia and the Netherlands. Foreign Minister of Nepal, Shisir Khanal, informed the House of Representatives that 80 security personnel, including 44 Nepal Army personnel, have gone missing from various locations. The flash flood damaged eight operational hydropower projects with a total capacity of 354 megawatts and five under-construction projects located in the Nuwakot and Rasuwa districts. Nineteen motorable bridges have been washed away. Nepalese Army, Armed Police Force and Nepal Police personnel have been mobilised in the affected areas to carry out rescue and relief work. Chinese President Xi Jinping ordered all-out efforts to search for and rescue missing people. A total of 145 officers and soldiers from the Xigaze detachment of the People’s Armed Police have been sent to the affected border port to assist with emergency response operations. Mr Xi also stressed the need to strengthen monitoring and early warning, ensure scientific rescue operations and guard against secondary disasters. Nepalese President Ramchandra Paudel has expressed sorrow over the loss of lives and property due to the flash flood.

The procurement operation commenced on the 15th of May and around 1.21 LMT of onions have been procured for the buffer. national_raw_news.content: Power ministers of the Northeastern states have sought greater financial assistance from the Centre for modernising the regional power grid and implementing key projects to improve electricity supply in the region, an official statement released yesterday said. The demand was raised at a meeting with Union Power Minister Manohar Lal Khattar in New Delhi on Tuesday. Led by North Eastern Regional Power Committee (NERPC) Chairman and Meghalaya Power Minister Metbah Lyngdoh, the delegation included Mizoram Power Minister F Rodingliana, Arunachal Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Chowna Mein and senior officials from the northeastern states. The ministers urged the Centre to provide the funds required for grid modernisation and sought special assistance for projects already submitted by the states under the Power System Development Fund (PSDF), following changes in the scheme’s implementation, the statement said. They also highlighted priority projects for the region, including Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) or Energy Management System (EMS) and Emergency Restoration System (ERS), and sought central support for their implementation, it said. The ministers apprised of the difficulties faced by the Northeastern states in executing power infrastructure projects due to the region’s challenging terrain. They said that long transmission lines are often required to supply electricity to remote and scattered settlements, making reliable power supply difficult and stressed the need for additional substations in far-flung areas. Rodingliana urged Khattar to formulate a mechanism for more transparent and effective utilisation of the 10 per cent Gross Budgetary Support (GBS) earmarked for the Northeast by 54 Union ministries. He also sought a larger allocation from the 10 per cent GBS specifically for development of the power sector in the region. Khattar said he would take up the funding requirements raised by the Northeastern states with the Union Finance Minister, according to the statement. However, he noted that the Centre may not be able to bear the entire cost of all proposed projects and the states would also have to contribute, it said. The states’ capacity to contribute would have to be assessed before a comprehensive proposal is prepared and pursued with the Ministry of Finance, Khattar said. The Union Power Minister also urged the states to expedite the ongoing installation of smart meters and stressed the need for “check meters” to help consumers verify and understand smart-meter readings. He further called for sustained efforts to reduce transmission losses and promote commercialisation in the power sector wherever feasible. The NERPC was constituted under the Ministry of Power in accordance with the Electricity Act, 2003, and comprises the seven Northeastern states. Its chairmanship rotates among the member states.
